pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🧩 **Strand 4 — Computational Thinking**
Sub-strand 4: Artificial Intelligence

When your phone unlocks by recognising your face, when a map app predicts traffic, or when a chatbot answers your question, artificial intelligence is at work. In this unit you will learn general definitions of the key AI technologies and discuss how AI is used in society.

pages.title: Areas and Applications of Artificial Intelligence
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.4.4.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- give general definitions of key AI technologies;
- compare the key technologies;
- discuss the uses and importance of AI to society.
**Artificial Intelligence (AI)** is the ability of computers and machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as recognising speech and images, understanding language, making decisions, learning from experience and solving problems.
[[fig:c7-f22|Figure 21: How AI, machine learning, neural networks and deep learning are related]]

pages.title: Key AI and related technologies (general definitions)
pages.body:
## Key AI and related technologies (general definitions)
| **Technology** | **General definition** | **Example** |
|---|---|---|
| Machine Learning (ML) | A branch of AI in which computers **learn patterns from data** and improve with experience, instead of following only fixed rules. | Email spam filters; YouTube recommendations |
| Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) | Computer systems loosely modelled on the **neurons of the human brain**: layers of connected “nodes” that pass signals and learn by adjusting the strength of connections. | Handwriting and face recognition |
| Deep Learning | Machine learning using ANNs with **many layers** (“deep” networks); very good at images, sound and language. | Voice assistants; AI chatbots; medical image analysis |
| Data Mining and Analytics | Searching large amounts of data to discover useful patterns, trends and relationships to support decisions. | A supermarket finding which items customers buy together |
| Virtual Reality (VR) | A completely computer-generated 3D world that the user experiences through a headset and can move around in. | VR games; flight and driving simulators; virtual field trips |
| Augmented Reality (AR) | Digital images or information **laid over the real world**, usually through a phone camera or smart glasses. | Snapchat/Instagram filters; Google Lens; Pokémon GO |
| Mixed Reality (MR) | A blend of the real and virtual worlds in which digital objects can **interact** with real surroundings in real time. | Microsoft HoloLens; Apple Vision Pro |
| Gamification | Using game elements (points, badges, levels, leaderboards) in non-game activities to motivate people. | Duolingo streaks; Khan Academy energy points; loyalty points |

pages.title: Key AI and related technologies (general definitions) (continued)
pages.body:
[[fig:c7-f23|Figure 22: From the real world to fully virtual reality]]
> ⏳ **Then and now — WHAT YOU WILL SEE TODAY Generative AI** Since late 2022, **generative AI** tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot, which create text, images and code from instructions, have become widely used. They are powerful learning aids, but they can make mistakes and invent facts. Always check their answers, never submit AI-written work as your own, and follow your school’s rules on using AI.
## Uses and importance of AI to society
| **Sector** | **Use of AI** |
|---|---|
| Health | Analysing X-rays and scans to detect diseases early; predicting outbreaks; health chatbots |
| Agriculture | Apps that identify crop diseases from a photo of a leaf; weather and yield prediction |
| Education | Personalised learning apps; automatic marking; translation and reading assistance |
| Finance | Detecting fraud in Mobile Money and bank transactions; credit scoring |
| Transport | Navigation apps predicting traffic; self-driving cars |
| Communication | Speech recognition, translation, voice assistants |
| Security | Face recognition, CCTV analysis, spam and malware detection |
| Intelligent robots | Robots that see, move, and respond to speech in factories, hospitals and homes |
> 🇬🇭 **Ghana connection** In 2019 Google opened its first AI research centre in Africa in **Accra**, working on problems such as crop disease detection and language technology for African languages.

pages.title: Key AI and related technologies (general definitions) (continued)
pages.body:
> 💡 **Think About It Responsible Ai** AI can be **biased** if it learns from unfair data; it can be used to spread fake images and videos (**deepfakes**); and it raises questions about privacy and jobs. How can Ghana make sure AI benefits everyone?
> 🧪 **Activity**
Watch a video or look at pictures of intelligent robots and AI in use (e.g. a humanoid robot, a self-driving car, a surgical robot). In groups, list the AI technologies each one uses and present how it benefits society.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Define artificial intelligence.
2. Compare virtual reality, augmented reality and mixed reality.
3. Explain the difference between machine learning and deep learning.
4. Discuss **four** uses of AI in Ghana.
5. State **two** concerns about AI and how they can be reduced.
